items.title: How to kill a djinn and get away with it: The Figure in the Fog by Manini Brar
items.summary: On a balmy night in May 1958, in a small village in Balasore district in Orissa, a Nepali man called Ram Bahadur Thapa stabbed and killed a ghost. This is not a made up story. Reality, as they say, is often stranger than fiction. Ghosts aren't real, of course, but Ram Bahadur believed in good faith that he was indeed attacking ghosts. The ghosts were in fact village women gathering flowers and the attack left one woman dead and the others severely injured. Ram Bahadur was tried and acquitted by a trial court which held that widespread local superstition among the Adivasi communities in the area made his mistaken belief a genuine defence under the mistake-of-fact provision (Section 79) of the erstwhile Indian Penal Code. This is one of the themes in The Figure in the Fog: Malti Jakhar Case Files , authored by Manini Brar , who writes about a fictional tribal village called Pitthoo whose inhabitants believe that a djinn haunts their forest. But Brar manages to make the case surprisingly relevant to a contemporary audience, even one far removed from the world of law. items.title: Detention v. arrest: Beyond labels
items.summary: The distinction between detention and arrest is often treated as a matter of terminology. In practice, however, it concerns something far more fundamental: the extent to which the State can deprive an individual of personal liberty while avoiding the procedural safeguards that the law attaches to an arrest. The terms custody, detention and arrest are often used interchangeably in ordinary speech, but the law places each at a different point on the same spectrum of restraint. 'Custody' is the widest of the three. As the Supreme Court held in Niranjan Singh v. Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote , a person is in custody the moment they submit to the control of the police or the court, whether or not any formal arrest has been recorded. ‘Arrest’ is the narrowest and most consequential of the three, since it requires an accusation or suspicion of an offence and, once made, immediately triggers the full suite of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) safeguards. ‘Detention’ sits between the two: it is custody exercised without an accusation, whether for brief inquiry under BNSS Section 170 , through the security proceedings in BNSS Sections 125 to 129 , or, in its most severe executive f

In an order passed on July 23, Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale set aside a Patna High Court judgment as well as the Bihar government's order rejecting a widow's request for compassionate appointment for her daughter following her husband's death. items.summary: The High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh on Friday observed that courts cannot deny bail to a person accused of a crime only to “teach him a lesson” or to satisfy the conscience of society [ Nisar Ahmed Joo v. UT of J&K ]. Justice Sanjay Dhar explained that such an approach would amount to pre-trial punishment, which is impermissible in law. The Court made the observation while granting bail to a man accused of raping a girl aged around 16-17 years old in 2024. The Court granted him bail after noting that the allegations against him appeared to be highly doubtful. "Merely because the petitioner is facing trial for heinous offences which entail punishment extending upto life imprisonment, is not a good enough reason to deny concession of bail to him when his, prima facie, involvement in the alleged crime is highly doubtful. The concession of bail to the petitioner, in these circumstances, cannot be denied just to teach him a lesson or to satisfy the conscience of the society as it would amount to inflicting pre-trial punishment upon them, which is impermissible in law," the Court said. Saurashtra Aaj Tak and Another ]. Justice Mini Pushkarna directed the newspaper to adopt another name that is neither similar nor deceptively similar to the ‘Aaj Tak’ mark owned by TV Today Network. The Court observed that the words ‘Aaj Tak’ had acquired a secondary meaning and had become distinctive of the news dissemination services offered by TV Today Network. “ The manner of the use of the words ‘Saurashtra Aaj Tak’, with more emphasis on the words ‘Aaj Tak’, leaves no doubt that the respondent/defendant (the newspaper) is trying to pass off its newspaper on the goodwill and reputation of the appellant/plaintiff (TV Today), ” the Court added. Justice Mini Pushkarna The July 30 judgment came in an appeal filed by TV Today against a February 2012 decision of a Delhi trial court. items.title: Delhi riots: Sessions court sentences Tahir Hussain to life in jail for murder of IB officer Ankit Sharma
items.summary: A Delhi court on Friday sentenced former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) councillor Tahir Hussain and four other convicts to life imprisonment for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the Delhi Riots of 2020. Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Parveen Singh of the Karkardooma Court rejected the prosecution's plea for death penalty and instead sentenced the five convicts to life in jail. The Court said that while the barbarity of the crime was "nauseating and sickening", the convicts -- Tahir Hussain, Nazir, Asim, Javed and Anas -- are not beyond reformation. It observed that the crime was committed when Delhi was going through communal riots, and it shows utmost brutality. It said that Sharma was sucked in by a murderous mob baying for blood. “The savagery did not end there [with the murder of Sharma]. Instead, the body was strapped like an animal as if the hatred has still not satiated. The body was then thrown into the nallah (drain). The barbarity with which this horrendous crime was committed, is nauseating and sickening. items.title: Rajasthan police tells High Court it will close cheating case against Sanjay Leela Bhansali, others
items.summary: Rajasthan Police has decided to file a closure report in a cheating case registered last year against filmmaker Sanjay Leela Bhansali and two members of his production team in connection with the film Love & War starring Ranbir Kapoor, Vicky Kaushal and Alia Bhatt. The information was submitted made before Justice Baljinder Singh Sandhu in Rajasthan High Court on July 17 during the hearing of a petition moved by the three accused for quashing of the First Information Report (FIR). State counsel said the police after thorough investigation in the matter has proposed to file a negative final report before the competent court. The filing of a negative final report indicates that the investigating agency has not found sufficient material to prosecute the accused. The trial court will now consider whether to accept the police report or not. In view of the submission, the High Court declined to entertain proceed further with the petition filed by Bhansali, production manager Utkarsh Bali and Arvinder Gill for quashing the case. “ This Court has considered the matter and in view thereof, is not inclined to interfere in the matter," the Bench said while dismissing the plea by the accused.

items.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Poll wins of 6 more MLAs challenged before Kerala High Court
items.summary: Petitions have been filed before the Kerala High Court challenging the election victories of six Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) in the 2026 Kerala Assembly Elections. The elections of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) State President R ajeev Chandrashekhar , BJP leader V Muraleedharan , CPI(M)’s C Ravindranath and NK Akbar and Congress MLAs Rajan J Pallan and Reji Cheriyan have been challenged. The petitions, which accuse the victorious candidates of having engaged in corrupt practices during their election campaigns, were listed before various Benches on Friday. Since defects were flagged in the petitions, the Court has mostly given time for such defects to be cured and adjourned the cases for hearings from next week onwards. The petition challenging the election win of MLA Rajeev Chandrashekhar from the Nemom constitutency has been filed by Congress leader KS Sabarinadhan. Chandrashekhar had won the seat by defeating CPI (M)'s V Sivankutty by 4,978 votes. The matter was heard by Justice Ziyad Rahman AA today, who has listed it next on August 18. items.title: Kerala HC stays BCI orders constituting interim authority to carry out Bar Council of Kerala functions
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday stayed two orders issued by the Chairman of the Bar Council of India (BCI) constituting an interim authority to carry out certain functions of the Bar Council of Kerala (BCK) until the recently elected XIIIth State Council conducts its first meeting [ Yeshwanth Shenoy v Bar Council of India ]. One of the newly elected BCK members, advocate Yeshwanth Shenoy, has questioned how such an interim arrangement can continue after the newly elected council (XIII Bar Council of Kerala) was notified in the Kerala Gazette on June 16, 2026. Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas today agreed to hear two connected writ petitions, including the one by Shenoy, challenging the interim arrangement put in place by the BCI chairman. The Court also stayed the operation of the BCI orders setting up the interim authority. " This Court is prima facie satisfied that the impugned orders in these writ petitions, that is Exhibit P6 in W.P.(C) No.25168 of 2026 and Exhibits P10 and P11 in W.P.(C) No.26232 of 2026, have been issued without application of mind and against the scheme of the Advocates Act, " the Court stated.
